body: Terence Snooks, of Eastwood, was convicted at Basildon Magistrates’ Court on 1 September of 15 offences under section 9 of the Animal Welfare Act 2006, Southend-on-Sea City Council says. The case came after council and police officers removed 15 German shepherd dogs from a property in Eastwood in February 2025, following residents’ complaints about persistent barking and the state of the property.

The council says the dogs lacked proper food, fresh water, bedding, exercise and socialisation, and the house and garden were heavily contaminated with faeces and urine. Many of the animals had matted fur and overgrown claws, several were underweight, and three were so badly affected that they had to be put to sleep. Five went to a specialist breed rehabilitation centre and most of the rest have been rehomed.

ITV News reported the case on Wednesday. Snooks is due to be sentenced at Basildon Magistrates’ Court on 8 December. Councillor Irene Ferguson said the result showed the council would act on serious welfare concerns.

official.headline: Colchester asks residents where to save money in 2027/28 budget
official.summary: Colchester City Council's budget survey runs until 9am on 14 December, with rising homelessness costs among the pressures it lists.
body: Colchester City Council opened its consultation on the 2027/28 budget on Monday 16 November, asking residents where it should cut, spend more or work differently. It names rising costs, steady demand for services and the growing cost of supporting people facing homelessness as the main pressures.

Councillor William Sunnucks, portfolio holder for resources, said: "We need your views on where we can save money." The answers will shape priorities for services including bin collections, parks, leisure, housing and community safety. People can fill in the online survey or attend a Residents' Panel session at the Town Hall from 10am to noon on Tuesday 8 December, or from 7pm to 8.30pm on Thursday 10 December.
Cabinet looks at the first draft budget position on Wednesday 2 December, and the consultation closes at 9am on Monday 14 December. Full Council sets the final budget in February 2027.

body: Luc Benkenstein has left Essex by mutual agreement and will join Durham as part of the deal, the club announced on Thursday 19 November.

The all-rounder arrived at Chelmsford in 2021 and made his debut that season in the One Day Cup, against Durham. He went on to play 80 times for Essex across all formats, and had signed a contract extension that ran until the end of the 2027 season.

Truro forward Luke Jephcott saw an eighth-minute effort scrambled away after a Christian Oxlade-Chamberlain long throw, and a Will Dean header from a set piece was also cleared on the line. After the break the home attack rarely troubled teenage Billericay goalkeeper Khari Ranson, and late on Jephcott tracked back to stop Jamie Mauge from shooting.

The result keeps Truro fourth, four points behind leaders Ebbsfleet United with a game in hand, The Post reported. Billericay host Slough Town on Saturday 21 November before a trip to Ebbsfleet on Tuesday 24 November.

Ramsgate led inside two minutes when Raphe Brown headed in after Brentwood goalkeeper Aiden Prall had saved a Billy Munday header. Alfie Paxman struck from the edge of the area for the second, then set up Callum Jones for the third before the break. Prall kept the margin down by stopping a Paxman penalty shortly before the hour.

At The Dripping Pan, Stanway followed a goalless home draw with Whitehawk a week earlier with another shut-out, a result that lifted them off the bottom of the division. body: Gymnasts Emily and Abigail Roper have returned to the University of Essex, where they study Sports and Exercise Science at the Colchester campus, after making Commonwealth Games history for Wales, the university reports. The 21-year-old twins were back on campus in their Essex Blades kit, holding up their Team Wales shirts from Glasgow 2026.

The sisters joined Essex on a sports scholarship in autumn 2025 with Glasgow as their goal. They train at Pipers Vale Gymnastics Club in Ipswich and also compete for the Essex Blades in student competitions, where Emily won gold and Abigail bronze at the BUCS championships in February.

body: A crash on the clockwise A282 in Thurrock shut the QEII Bridge at the Dartford Crossing for around three hours on Friday 20 November, and two people were taken to hospital, Brentwood Live reported.

The East of England Ambulance Service said it was called at 10.30am to a collision on the M25 near junction 31, on the approach to the bridge. It sent two ambulances, an ambulance officer, a rapid response vehicle and Essex & Herts Air Ambulance, and two patients were taken by road to the Royal London Hospital.

Firefighters freed the two people, who were trapped in their vehicles, and handed them to paramedics, the Echo reported. Essex Police said four vehicles were involved; the Echo reported that they included two lorries and a car, and that the air ambulance landed on a grass verge near junction 30.

Queues built up across south Essex. At about 12.15pm, National Highways' overhead signs showed the M25 closed at junction 30 and delays of more than an hour between junctions 29 and 1A. By the afternoon, the AA was reporting delays of about 20 minutes on the bridge and about 29 minutes for traffic heading to junction 30 from junction 27, according to Brentwood Live.

More closures are planned at the crossing. The west tunnel, which carries northbound traffic, is due to close from 9pm tonight until 5.30am on Saturday, according to National Highways' roadworks data. National Highways has also confirmed the QEII Bridge will close from 10.30pm on Saturday until 5.30am on Sunday, London Now reported.
The condition of the two people taken to hospital has not been released. This story will be updated.

stories.headline: Essex anti-social behaviour reports up 76% as robbery falls 19%
stories.summary: A Seax analysis of police.uk data shows anti-social behaviour reports rose in 50 of Essex Police's 56 neighbourhood areas, with Basildon recording the most.
body: Police in Essex logged 2,042 reports of anti-social behaviour in September 2026, up from 1,162 in September 2025, according to the street-level records published on police.uk. Recorded crime rose more slowly, to 12,530 from 11,563. Both figures were lower than in August.
Some of the rise in anti-social behaviour may come from changes in how police record it, rather than from more incidents. The figures do not show how much.

Violence and sexual offences remain by far the largest category of crime. Police recorded 5,800 of them in September, up 15% from 5,045 a year earlier, and they made up almost half of all recorded crime in the county.
Thefts rose too. Shoplifting went up 22% to 1,265 offences, theft from the person rose by half to 126, and other theft climbed 20% to 1,008.

Most other types of crime fell. Robbery dropped 19%, from 132 to 107, and bicycle theft fell 12% to 94. Criminal damage and arson went down 8% to 981, vehicle crime 6% to 851 and burglary 3% to 376. Drug offences, public order offences and possession of weapons were also slightly lower.

Anti-social behaviour reports rose in 50 of Essex Police's 56 neighbourhood areas. Basildon had the most, with 151 reports against 76 a year earlier, followed by Colchester Town West with 112 and Southend Central with 110.

Among the 10 areas with the most reports, three more than doubled their totals: Chelmsford Town, from 38 to 86; Chafford Hundred and Grays, from 51 to 107; and Colchester Town East, from 36 to 75. Only one of the 10, Aveley and Ockendon, saw a fall, from 57 to 54.

Taking crime and anti-social behaviour together, records rose in 45 neighbourhoods and fell in 11. Clacton had the biggest rise, with 151 more records than a year earlier, followed by Westcliff (129 more), Basildon (118 more) and Chelmsford South (115 more). In Westcliff, shoplifting nearly trebled.
The biggest falls were in Wakering, with 21 fewer records, Thundersley, with 19 fewer, and Canvey, with 18 fewer.

Police.uk's anti-social behaviour category covers personal, environmental and nuisance anti-social behaviour. It is recorded separately from crime and is not part of the official recorded crime statistics.
Anti-social behaviour and crimes that are not emergencies can be reported to Essex Police online at essex.police.uk or by calling 101. Call 999 if a crime is happening now or someone is in danger.

Police.uk places each record at an approximate location rather than an exact address. The Seax counted every record inside the boundaries of the 56 neighbourhood areas. A few records sit exactly on the line between two neighbourhoods and appear in both neighbourhoods' figures, but each is counted once in the county totals. A further 216 crimes in September had no location and are not included. Totals may differ slightly from Essex Police's own figures.

stories.headline: NHS Essex looks for new online consultation tools for 204 GP surgeries
stories.summary: Suppliers can show their systems at an online event on 9 December, and a two-year contract is due to start in spring 2027.
body: NHS Essex is looking for new software to handle online consultations at the 204 GP surgeries it covers, and has asked suppliers to show what their systems can do before it decides what to buy.

The integrated care board, which plans and pays for NHS services for about 1.9 million people in Essex, wants a contract lasting two years, PublicTechnology reported on Friday 20 November. The notice does not say how much it is worth.

Online consultations let patients contact their surgery through its website, to describe a problem or ask for advice, and the request goes straight to the practice. At the moment, Essex surgeries use a range of different systems, chosen to suit local needs, the notice says.

The board says practices with similar needs could be grouped together when it buys the new service, so not every surgery would necessarily end up with the same system. Nothing has been decided yet: not what it needs, how it will buy it or which company will win.

This first step is what the Procurement Act 2023 calls preliminary market engagement. Suppliers can demonstrate their systems at an online event on 9 December, where GP practices and the board can ask questions, and must register by 3 December. Taking part gives a company no advantage when the contract is later put out to tender, the notice says.

The plans come weeks after a problem with a website provider left some GP practice websites and online consultation services in north east Essex unavailable. NHS Essex said on 28 October that practices remained open, and pointed patients to the NHS App, Pharmacy First, phoning or emailing their practice, NHS 111, and 999 in a life-threatening emergency.
Any change to the systems patients use would not come before spring 2027, when the new contract is due to begin.
points: Supplier registration closes on 3 December
NHS Essex serves about 1.9 million people
No decision yet on the system or supplier

stories.summary: Two new scanners at the Chelmsford hospital will help doctors find and track cancer, Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust says.
body: The suite is in the Nuclear Medicine department at Broomfield Hospital, the trust announced on Friday 20 November.

Doctors use these scans to plan cancer treatment as well as to diagnose the disease and check how it is responding. The machines are also used to investigate kidney and urinary conditions, the trust said.

Also used for kidney and urinary checks

stories.headline: Essex weekend travel: buses replace trains from Colchester on Sunday
stories.summary: Rail passengers on the main line and the Braintree branch face replacement buses, and the QEII Bridge at the Dartford Crossing shuts overnight on Saturday 21 November.
body: On Sunday 22 November buses replace Greater Anglia trains between Colchester and Ingatestone for London journeys, and between Colchester and Chelmsford for the stations in between, Network Rail says. Buses also run instead of trains between Braintree and Witham and between Sudbury and Marks Tey on both Saturday 21 and Sunday 22 November, and Bures station stays shut until 4am on Monday 23 November.

On the roads, National Highways shuts the QEII Bridge at the Dartford Crossing from 10pm on Saturday 21 November to 6am on Sunday, with diversions via the other crossings. In Witham, Newland Street closes from noon to 8pm on Saturday for the Christmas Fayre, and First Essex's 371 bus will not serve the Mill Lane, Newland Street and The George stops. In Wickford, Runwell Road shuts from 8pm on Sunday to 5am on Monday for roadworks, and the X10 cannot serve the town while it is closed.

In Ongar, Fyfield Road stays closed for roadworks until Monday 23 November, with First Essex's 46 on a diversion. From Monday 23 to Thursday 26 November the Dartford Crossing's west tunnel shuts from 9pm to 5.30am each night. The following weekend, 28 and 29 November, buses replace trains between Southminster and Wickford.

Bures station shut until 4am on Monday 23 November
Dartford west tunnel shut nightly from 23 to 26 November

stories.headline: Essex opticians treat new eye problems without a GP visit, NHS Essex says
stories.summary: The free Minor Eye Conditions Service runs at participating opticians across the county and can save patients a trip to A&E.
body: Jayne Mason's mother had a red, painful eye and was thinking about going to A&E, NHS Essex said on Friday 20 November. Her usual optician had no appointment, so Ms Mason found a practice in Pitsea taking part in the Minor Eye Conditions Service. After a short phone assessment her mother was seen within 30 minutes and told nothing was seriously wrong.

The free service runs at participating opticians across Essex, with no GP referral needed. It covers new problems such as red or sore eyes, dry or gritty eyes, swelling, watery eyes, new flashes or floaters, eye pain, ingrowing eyelashes and grit in the eye. In a survey of 641 patients in mid and south Essex between April and June 2026, 96% said they would recommend it, and 20% said they would otherwise have gone to A&E.

Dr Boye Tayo, clinical lead for eye care at NHS Essex, said the board wants more people to know the service exists. Patients should call a participating practice first rather than turn up. NHS Essex says anyone who suddenly loses sight, has severe eye pain, a serious eye injury or a strong chemical in the eye should go to A&E or call 999.
points: No GP referral needed
Appointments within 24 hours or a few working days, depending on symptoms
35% of surveyed patients would otherwise have seen their GP

stories.headline: Tendring offers £100,000+ in health grants to sport and community groups
stories.summary: Clubs and groups across the Tendring district can bid for money for projects that get people active, eating well or looking after their mental health.
body: Sports clubs and community groups in the Tendring district have until Sunday 3 January 2027 to apply, Tendring District Council said on Friday 20 November. Bids can cover active travel, club development and disability sport, sport for young children and after school, food and nutrition for families, or mental health.

The council says more than £110,000 is on offer in all. The money comes from its sports strategy budget and public health funding, with a share from the Love Clacton Town Board, part of the government's Pride in Place scheme. Councillor Mick Barry, cabinet member for sport and leisure, said 'just a little bit of cash can really kick-start something fantastic'. Councillor Gina Placey, cabinet member for partnerships, said being active helps mental health and can ease loneliness.

Groups can find out how to apply at free Sports Forum evenings. They are at the Columbine Centre in Walton-on-the-Naze on Thursday 26 November at 6pm, Mistley Parish Hall on Tuesday 1 December at 6.15pm, Dovercourt Bay Lifestyles Leisure Centre on Friday 4 December at 6pm and Brightlingsea Parish Hall on Monday 7 December at 6pm. Applications go through the Tendring Leisure website.
points: Applications close on 3 January 2027
Love Clacton Town Board adds to the pot
Advice evenings in Walton, Mistley, Dovercourt and Brightlingsea

stories.headline: Three Colchester food outlets hold hygiene ratings of 0 or 1
stories.summary: A High Street restaurant has the lowest rating, zero, and two other city centre businesses are rated one after inspections in October, an analysis of Food Standards Agency data by The Seax shows.
body: Bees Indian Restaurant & Bar at 105 High Street, Colchester, is rated 0, which the Food Standards Agency describes as urgent improvement necessary, after an inspection on 14 October 2026. King of Spice, a takeaway at 59 East Street, is rated 1, meaning major improvement necessary, after an inspection on 6 October. Vinny's Restaurant at 1 Headgate is also rated 1 after a visit on 8 October.

The ratings are those shown on the Food Standards Agency's website on 20 November and reflect what Colchester City Council inspectors found on those dates. Each business can appeal, ask for a re-inspection once it has made improvements, or publish its own reply on the ratings website. The published data gives scores only, not the inspectors' notes, so it does not show what the problems were.

Across Colchester low ratings are rare. Of 1,413 rated premises in the city council's area, 0.9% have a rating of 0, 1 or 2 and 90.7% have the top rating of 5. In Rochford and Tendring the share of low ratings is above 4%, although councils inspect at different rates, so the figures are a guide rather than a league table. Every rating can be checked at ratings.food.gov.uk.
points: Figures collected by The Seax data desk on 20 November 2026
Colchester City Council carried out all three visits
A rating of 5 means hygiene standards are very good

stories.summary: South West Essex Community Education Trust wants to build a sports hall with two padel courts at William Edwards School in Grays, open to public bookings in the evenings.
body: The hall, almost 10 metres high, would replace part of the car park and service area at the Stifford Clays Road school, cutting parking from 53 spaces to 43, Your Thurrock reports. The trust says booking income would pay for upkeep of the school's sports facilities.
The site is in the Metropolitan Green Belt, and the trust argues the benefits to pupils and the community amount to very special circumstances. Thurrock Council has not yet decided the application.
points: Public opening until 10pm on weekdays, 9pm on Saturdays and 6pm on Sundays
Separate from the 54 homes approved nearby off Blackshots Lane in October

stories.headline: Thurrock Council's Inspire careers team up for national inclusion award
stories.summary: Thurrock Council's Inspire Employability and Skills team is shortlisted for Inclusive Team of the Year at the Inspiring Women in Local Government Awards 2026.
body: Inspire gives careers advice to Thurrock residents of all ages, with help on jobs, training, volunteering, housing, money and wellbeing, and focuses on people who find it hard to get into work or education, Your Thurrock reports. Its advisers are all qualified to at least Level 6.

The winners are due to be announced on Wednesday 2 December 2026. Councillor Milena Bingley, Thurrock's cabinet member for education and skills, said the council was proud of what the team had achieved.
points: The service is Matrix accredited
Residents can be referred through the Thurrock Council website

stories.headline: Colchester Castle roof repairs finished after £1.3m project
stories.summary: Colchester City Council says work to stop water getting into the Norman keep has been completed.
body: Repairs to the roof of Colchester Castle, the largest Norman keep in Europe, have been completed, BBC News reported on Friday 20 November. The Grade I listed building had been letting in water as it aged.

Surveys found the north-west tower was the most badly damaged part. Work began early in 2026 under the eye of Historic England, paid for mainly by a grant of £1,293,625 from the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport.
points: Work overseen by Historic England
North-west tower was worst affected
Councillor Darius Laws leads on heritage for Colchester City Council

stories.headline: Clacton Hospital's £25m revamp brings new urgent care centre
stories.summary: Children's services and musculoskeletal therapy have also moved into the rebuilt space, with Tendring council paying £2m of the cost.
body: Tendring District Council's leader, Mark Stephenson, and deputy leader, Ivan Henderson, toured the rebuilt space at Clacton Hospital in the week to Friday 20 November. The council put £2m towards the £25m scheme, led by East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust.

The redeveloped area now houses an urgent treatment centre, community paediatrics, children's therapies and the musculoskeletal therapy service. NHS England and NHS Property Services also helped pay for the work. Paul Scott, chief executive of the hospital trust, welcomed the councillors on the visit.

The council's money came from Government-backed Community Regeneration Partnership funding, which also pays for projects in Clacton and Jaywick Sands. Councillor Stephenson said it was about helping people get "first-class medical care close to home". The hospital has also gained a community diagnostic centre, an endoscopy suite and a new birthing suite.
points: Council money came through the Community Regeneration Partnership
Paul Scott is chief executive of the hospital trust
Podiatry and the Jubilee Infusion Lounge have also moved to new space

stories.headline: Stansted Airport plans major emergency exercise with 400 taking part
stories.summary: London Stansted will rehearse its response to an aircraft accident using a decommissioned plane, and the airport says flights should not be affected.
body: The full-scale exercise takes place on Tuesday 24 November at the airport's Compass Base remote stand, London Stansted said on 20 November. Civil Aviation Authority rules require one at least every four years.

Crews from Essex Police, Essex County Fire and Rescue Service, East of England Ambulance Service and Essex & Herts Air Ambulance will join airport staff. People living nearby may see more emergency vehicles than usual.
points: Uttlesford District Council, Essex County Council and the British Red Cross are supporting it
The Air Accident Investigation Branch, Border Force and Ryanair are also involved

stories.headline: Harlow's Avant Garde salon on The Rows shuts without warning
stories.summary: Clients of the long-running Harlow town centre hair and beauty salon found its doors shut this week.
body: Staff at Avant Garde Hair and Beauty, on The Rows above the market square, were told by text that the business had closed and to contact the management company about equipment left there, Your Harlow reported on Friday 20 November.

Some clients had regular bookings and reacted with anger and confusion. Your Harlow said the business had not replied to its questions, and that some people are in early talks about reopening the salon.
points: Salon had traded since the mid-1970s
Business did not answer Your Harlow's questions

stories.headline: Harlow to switch on bigger Christmas lights display on Broad Walk
stories.summary: Harlow Council says this year's town centre display is bigger and brighter than before, with lights across more of the town.
body: The switch-on is on Broad Walk at 4pm on Saturday 21 November, with live entertainment, festive music and food and drink stalls. It opens Harlow Council's Christmas Extravaganza programme for the town.

Harlow on Ice, the town's seasonal skating rink, opens on the same day. A Christmas market follows from Saturday 12 December to Sunday 20 December, open 10am to 6pm daily, with stalls along Broad Walk and in Market Square.
The council has not said who will switch on the lights or whether any roads will close. Details of the wider programme are on its Christmas in Harlow website.
points: Event starts at 4pm
Christmas market open 10am to 6pm daily
Run by Harlow Council

stories.headline: Grays scrapyard fire likely started by discarded battery, crews say
stories.summary: Essex County Fire and Rescue Service believes a thrown-away battery started the Little Thurrock scrapyard fire. About 20 firefighters had it out by 8.50pm on 19 November.
body: About 80 tonnes of scrap metal was burning when crews reached the yard off Rectory Road, Little Thurrock, at 6.08pm on Thursday 19 November. After putting it out, firefighters worked with site staff to break up the scrap and check for hotspots. They left at 9.30pm.

Station Manager Rick Williams said batteries can catch fire if they are damaged or crushed. He asked people to take used batteries to a recycling centre or collection point, and never to put them in a skip or with general rubbish.

Smoke from the fire drifted across Grays during the evening, and neighbours were told to keep their windows shut. The yard is on the Globe Industrial Estate, close to homes, where six fire crews fought a building fire in June 2022.
points: About 80 tonnes of scrap was alight
Crews left the scene at 9.30pm
Recycling sites are listed at loveessex.org

stories.headline: Basildon councillors back permanent war memorial D-Day veteran sought
stories.summary: Basildon and Laindon have no permanent war memorial. Basildon Council has now voted unanimously to change that, taking up Don Sheppard's long campaign.
body: Basildon Council approved the proposal unanimously on 17 November, BBC News reports. Mayor Sam Journet proposed it and Conservative leader Andy Barnes seconded it.

No site, design or cost has been chosen yet. The council will consult the Royal British Legion, the Commonwealth War Graves Commission, veterans and Mr Sheppard's family, and the plans are expected to include a tribute to him. The Royal Engineer, who landed on D-Day, died aged 104 in 2024.
points: Proposed by mayor Sam Journet
Site, design and funding still to be decided
Don Sheppard died in 2024, aged 104

stories.headline: Colchester Hospital asks patients to hand back crutches and frames
stories.summary: The north Essex hospital trust cleans, checks and repairs returned walking aids so they can go to other patients.
body: East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust made the appeal on Friday 20 November. In Colchester, crutches, walking frames and metal walking sticks can go in the large blue recycling containers outside the hospital's front entrance, or outside the side doors of the Dame Clare Marx Building.

Equipment delivered to a patient's home, such as hospital beds, commodes, hoists and toilet frames, should carry a Medequip or ECL sticker. Medequip collects these free on 0333 034 2048, or they can be taken to its depot at Horizon 120 Business Park in Braintree.

The trust asks people not to take equipment to its community hospitals or community teams, which cannot accept it. Fabric moon boots and arm supports cannot be returned because they cannot be cleaned for reuse.
points: Ipswich Hospital has its own drop-off points
Unstickered items go back to the hospital team that supplied them

stories.headline: Abbotts Hall reserve near Colchester counts record number of rare moths
stories.summary: Essex Wildlife Trust has found more of a rare moth than ever before at its Abbotts Hall reserve after a conservation project there, the Daily Gazette reports.

stories.headline: Frosty Friday night for Essex with lows of -1C, then a bright Saturday
stories.summary: Freezing fog patches could slow early journeys on Saturday morning, and another cold night follows on Sunday. No Met Office weather warning is in force.
body: Temperatures are forecast to dip below freezing across inland Essex in the early hours of Saturday 21 November. The Met Office forecast for Chelmsford bottoms out at about 7am, Colchester is expected to be just as cold, and Harlow should hover a degree or so above zero. The Southend seafront stays milder, at about 2C. Fog is forecast to form after midnight almost everywhere, so drivers setting off early should allow time to clear windscreens.

Friday itself starts grey, with rain clearing south through the morning before a drier, cloudy afternoon and a high of about 9C. Skies then clear in the evening, which lets the cold set in. Saturday's fog should thin by late morning, leaving sunny spells, light winds and highs of 7C to 9C.

Sunday turns cloudier and breezier, with highs of 8C or 9C and a 20% to 30% chance of a shower. Temperatures fall back to about 0C inland on Sunday night. The Met Office outlook for the East of England says to expect overnight frosts until Monday, with temperatures near or slightly below average. Nights turn milder from Tuesday, with lows of about 6C.
points: Saturday's fog is forecast to lift by about 11am
Gusts of up to 28mph on Sunday
Milder nights return from Tuesday

stories.headline: NHS Essex urges flu jabs by 11 December for Christmas protection
stories.summary: Anyone across Essex who is eligible for a free flu vaccine and has not yet had it should book now, because the jab takes up to two weeks to work, NHS Essex says.
body: NHS Essex, the integrated care board for the whole county, said on Thursday 19 November that people who miss that date should still have the vaccine, because flu keeps circulating long after Christmas. Older people, pregnant women and people with some long-term health conditions face the greatest risk of serious illness.

Eligible adults can book through the NHS website or NHS App, call 119 free if they cannot book online, or ask their GP practice or a participating pharmacy, some of which take walk-ins. Children who were two or three on 31 August 2026 can have the vaccine at their GP practice or a pharmacy, and from 1 December pupils from Reception to Year 11 who missed the school round can go to a participating pharmacy.

Dr Matthew Sweeting, executive medical director at NHS Essex, asked families to fit the jab into their Christmas plans, since gatherings make flu easier to spread. More than 2 million people in the East of England have had a flu jab so far this season, said Dr Eleanor Powers of NHS England's regional team.
points: Call 119 if you cannot book online
Pregnant women can ask their midwife
School-age catch-up jabs at pharmacies from 1 December

stories.headline: Thurrock cabinet brings Tilbury Towns Fund board under council control
stories.summary: Thurrock Council's cabinet took over the running of the Tilbury Towns Fund board on Wednesday 18 November, despite protests from Thurrock MP Jen Craft.
body: The decision at the cabinet meeting on Wednesday 18 November hands the council control of how Tilbury's £22.8m of government regeneration money is managed, Thurrock Nub News reports. Thurrock MP Jen Craft had said she and the boards' chairs were told of the plan only days earlier. Cabinet member Milena Bingley called her accusations completely unfounded. Council officers had warned that changing governance could breach government funding rules.
points: Grays' board oversees £19.9m
Both boards were set up in January 2020 with private-sector chairs
Officers rated the funding clawback risk red

stories.headline: Tilbury community pantry and café get go-ahead as works go to tender
stories.summary: An empty building next to Tilbury Library in Civic Square is to become a volunteer-run food pantry and café, months later than Thurrock Council first hoped.
body: Thurrock Council's cabinet approved the tender for the building works on Wednesday 18 November, Thurrock Nub News reports. The scheme already has planning permission and is paid for from Tilbury's £22.8m Towns Fund. It copies the Purfleet Pantry, which has run for more than two years, and the library and community hub will also be improved. No opening date has been given.
points: First announced in June 2026, with an autumn opening hoped for
Cabinet member Tom Kelly says it will offer affordable food
The library works add digital and job-readiness space

stories.headline: Henham showhome wins national interior design award
stories.summary: A Bellway showhome in Henham, near Saffron Walden, has been named the best in the UK in a national interior design awards scheme.

stories.headline: Basildon firm AVRT trains soldiers and police in virtual reality
stories.summary: A three-person company in Basildon builds virtual reality training used by the British and Singaporean armies and trialled by UK police forces, The Standard reports.
body: AVRT, short for Adaptive Virtual Reality Training, works from an unassuming building in Basildon, where trainees wear modified headsets and carry a replica service rifle across foam mats, The Standard reported on 19 November. Enemies in its scenarios, such as a hostage rescue in a flat, can be run by a person or by an AI setting.
Sales director Andy Higgs said the US Marine Corps is due to receive an infantry trainer built on the system by the end of 2026, and that AI enemies are the next step.
points: Trainees can be tracked to within a millimetre and replayed in 3D
A haptic suit makes trainees feel simulated hits

stories.headline: Burnham-on-Crouch swimmers cross Channel in relay for Havens Hospices
stories.summary: Five friends from Burnham-on-Crouch have raised more than £9,000 for Havens Hospices by swimming a relay from England to France through the night.
body: James Cliff, Andrew Bell, Madeline Raymond, Clare Boston and Stuart Sargeant, who call themselves the Burnham Gang, finished their relay across the English Channel in 10 hours and 50 minutes, Havens Hospices announced on Thursday 19 November 2026. The route is about 21 miles through one of the world's busiest shipping lanes, in water of around 18C.
The group chose the challenge after visiting Fair Havens and Little Havens, the charity's hospices for adults and children in south Essex.
points: Relay time: 10 hours and 50 minutes
Swim of about 21 miles in water of around 18C
Havens needs more than £225,000 a week

stories.headline: c2c signalling fault near Barking disrupts trains on all routes
stories.summary: Passengers between Shoeburyness, Southend, Grays and London Fenchurch Street faced cancellations and delays of up to 20 minutes on the afternoon of Thursday 19 November.
body: A signalling system fault between West Ham and Barking disrupted c2c services on all routes on the afternoon of Thursday 19 November 2026, and the operator said it expected problems to last until 6pm. Trains could be cancelled, delayed or changed at short notice, c2c's JourneyCheck service said.

By about 3.30pm nine trains had been cancelled, including services from London Fenchurch Street, Shoeburyness, Southend Central and Leigh-on-Sea. West Ham High Level is not being served, one Shoeburyness train was ended at Upminster and several trains were diverted between Barking and Limehouse.

Extra trains added from Upminster
Updates promised at least hourly

stories.headline: Pitsea man jailed over gunpowder as judge says ChatGPT fed his fears
stories.summary: The Pitsea man said he was getting ready to protect his family in a 'post-apocalyptic scenario'. He was sentenced at Basildon Crown Court for illegally having explosive powder.
body: Ben Banham, 38, was jailed on Thursday 19 November over black powder found at his home in Pitsea, BBC News reports. More than 80 nearby homes were evacuated on 10 March. A jury cleared him in September of intending to cause harm.
Judge Shane Kollery KC said ChatGPT had fed Banham's anxiety. He accepted Banham meant no harm to the public, but said the powder was a real danger to others. Banham has already served eight months.
points: He was jailed for 28 months
Bomb disposal teams found a device in the house
Probation assessed him as low risk

stories.headline: Harlow hospital moves waiting list checks to My Alex Health app
stories.summary: Adults waiting for treatment at Princess Alexandra Hospital in Harlow will now get their 12-weekly waiting list questionnaire through the trust's own patient portal.
body: The questionnaires used to arrive through a system called Healthcare Communications Envoy; from now on patients will get a text from 'NHS PAHT' pointing them to My Alex Health, Princess Alexandra Hospital NHS Trust said on Thursday 19 November 2026. The trust says the switch makes its messages easier to recognise.

The two-minute questionnaire is sent every 12 weeks to eligible adults and lets them confirm whether they still need to be seen. The trust says anyone who does not fill it in will stay on the waiting list and their care will continue, and that a relative, friend or carer can help.
Patients not yet registered with My Alex Health will get a separate message on how to sign up. The trust plans a version for children and young people in future.
points: Sent every 12 weeks
Texts come from 'NHS PAHT'
Children's version planned

stories.headline: TG Jones to shut Harlow, Brentwood and Clacton shops
stories.summary: The former WH Smith high street chain plans to close its Harlow branch on 30 December and its Brentwood and Clacton branches on 12 January, ending their Post Office services, as the business is reviewed for sale.

stories.headline: Jaywick Sands' Brooklands could be rebuilt as one-way road with beach path
stories.summary: Tendring District Council has a preferred plan for the pothole-hit private road in Jaywick Sands, which residents named as their top priority for investment, but no decision has been taken.
body: Drainage work to stop the flooding that keeps opening potholes, a footpath on the beach side and westbound one-way traffic for vehicles are at the heart of Tendring District Council's preferred option for Brooklands in Jaywick Sands, announced on Thursday 19 November 2026. The plan also includes crossing points and traffic calming, and the council says residents, buses and essential services would keep their access.

Brooklands is an unadopted road that no council maintains. Tendring's cabinet agreed in March to look into improvements after the Jaywick Sands Place Plan made the road a key recommendation, and an independent road safety audit followed emergency pothole repairs earlier in 2026. Deputy leader Ivan Henderson said talks with residents made clear the road was among their highest priorities, while council leader Mark Stephenson said emergency repairs alone would not solve its longer-term problems.

Residents can see the plans and give their views at drop-in sessions at the Jaywick Community Resource Centre on Wednesday 2 December (2.30pm to 6pm), Golf Green Hall on Thursday 3 December (9.30am to 1pm) and the Sunspot during the Saturday market on 5 December (from 9am). Before any go-ahead, Tendring District Council needs legal powers usually held by Essex County Council, the highways authority, and talks between the two councils are continuing. The work would be paid for through the council's Community Regeneration Partnership with the Government.
points: Drop-in sessions on 2, 3 and 5 December
Bus operators, Essex Police and the Environment Agency were consulted
Essex County Council must hand over legal powers before work can start

stories.headline: NHS Essex asks patients not to demand antibiotics for colds and flu
stories.summary: Across Essex, the county's NHS integrated care board says rising resistance is making some infections harder to treat, and wants people to take antibiotics only when prescribed and exactly as directed.
body: England recorded an average of 406 antibiotic-resistant bloodstream infections every week in 2025, some of them life-threatening, NHS Essex said on Thursday 19 November 2026. Antibiotics treat bacterial illnesses such as pneumonia, meningitis and sepsis and are needed for surgery and some cancer care, but they do nothing against colds, flu or COVID-19.

Dr Matthew Sweeting, executive medical director at NHS Essex, asked people not to go to their GP expecting antibiotics for common illnesses, and to ask a pharmacist how to ease symptoms instead. Anyone prescribed a course should not save tablets for later or share them, and should take leftovers to a pharmacy for safe disposal, NHS Essex said.

NHS Essex also wants everyone eligible for flu, COVID-19 or RSV vaccines to book them, because fewer infections mean fewer antibiotics are needed. People can sign up to a personal pledge through the national Antibiotic Guardian campaign.
points: Antibiotics do not work on viruses
Leftover tablets can go back to any pharmacy
Antibiotic Guardian pledge open to all

stories.headline: Essex Police arrest 17 in week-long county lines crackdown
stories.summary: Eleven people were charged and remanded, and officers seized 22 throwing blades, a zombie knife, drugs and cash.
body: Seventeen people were arrested and 11 charged and remanded in custody during a week of intensified action against county lines drug networks, Essex Police said. Officers also returned three people wanted on recall to prison.

Crack cocaine, heroin and other drugs worth thousands of pounds were seized, along with at least £790 in cash and phones the force linked to drug supply. Officers recovered several weapons, including 22 throwing blades and a large zombie knife.

The force said the operation targeted networks linked to violence, weapons and the exploitation of vulnerable people, and that it would keep going after "the people and networks causing harm in our communities". Those charged are presumed innocent unless proven guilty.
points: Three people wanted on recall sent back to prison
Networks linked to the exploitation of vulnerable people

stories.headline: Harlow employment rate rises to 82.9% in latest ONS figures
stories.summary: Harlow is among the five best-performing areas in the country for jobs growth, according to Your Harlow's report on official labour market data.
body: The share of working-age people in jobs in Harlow has climbed by 15% over two years, Your Harlow reports, drawing on Office for National Statistics labour market figures published on Tuesday 17 November 2026. Employment minister Andrew Western called the figures a vote of confidence in the town's people and businesses.
points: UK unemployment rate fell to 4.6%
Figures came out as the Government backed Alan Milburn's youth jobs review

stories.headline: University of Essex experts lead call for coastal focus in mental health plan
stories.summary: Close to 150 researchers, health leaders and charities have signed a letter, coordinated from the University of Essex in Colchester, warning that England's new Mental Health Strategy could overlook coastal, rural and former industrial communities.
body: The letter to Alison McGovern, the minister for social care and mental health, is being coordinated by Professor Susan McPherson and Professor Victoria Bird of the university's Institute for Public Health and Wellbeing, the University of Essex announced on Thursday 19 November 2026. Their research found that young adults in the most deprived coastal areas are three times more likely to have undiagnosed mental distress than those in equally deprived inland areas.

Signatories include the chief executives of Mind, YoungMinds, Place2Be and the Centre for Mental Health, more than 60 professors and former care minister Sir Norman Lamb. Going by published affiliations, seven in ten contributors to the government's independent review of mental health conditions, ADHD and autism were based in London, Oxford or Cambridge, the letter notes. Professor McPherson said geography, as well as deprivation, can shape mental health outcomes.

The group wants the strategy to recognise geographical inequalities and to draw on research leaders, local partners and people with lived experience from the worst-affected places. It is also asking for funding so council public health teams can invest in community-led mental health work, and for the Prevention Concordat for Better Mental Health to be revived and refreshed.
points: Addressed to minister Alison McGovern
Coastal young adults three times likelier to have undiagnosed distress
Signed by more than 60 professors

stories.headline: Southend knife violence falls 23% but city still tops Essex list
stories.summary: Across Essex, serious violence involving knives has fallen 17% over two years, Essex Police says, while arrests for carrying knives rose 19% in the past 12 months.
body: Southend recorded 52 fewer reports of serious knife violence over the past 12 months, figures released by Essex Police on Thursday 19 November 2026 show, although the city still has more knife incidents than anywhere else in the county.

Extra patrols in six hotspot zones, paid for by the Home Office through the Police, Fire and Crime Commissioner for Essex, have led to 60 arrests since May in Chelmsford, Southend, Clacton, Colchester, Grays and Basildon. Over the past year a quarter of suspects and victims in Essex knife crime cases were aged 19 or under. Superintendent Darren Deex, the force's lead for knife crime, said officers "can't just arrest our way out of knife crime".

Officers are visiting schools and colleges this week as part of Operation Sceptre. Young people arrested for carrying a weapon can be referred to the Essex Violence and Vulnerability Unit, and 15 knife bins at police stations let people hand in blades safely. Roger Hirst, the Police, Fire and Crime Commissioner, chairs the Violence and Vulnerability Partnership.
points: 60 arrests since May from hotspot patrols in six towns
A quarter of knife crime suspects and victims were 19 or younger
15 knife bins at Essex police stations
stories.newAngle: Essex Police released new figures showing Southend's serious knife violence down 23% and 60 hotspot patrol arrests since May.

stories.headline: Harlow's River Way Bridge to shut to all vehicles
stories.summary: The River Way Bridge in Harlow is to close fully to traffic, the Daily Gazette reports.

stories.headline: Lakeside Retail Park to open King Living furniture showroom on Saturday
stories.summary: The family-owned Australian sofa and furniture maker is opening a two-floor store at West Thurrock, aimed at shoppers across Essex and east London.
body: King Living opens its showroom at Unit E2, Lakeside Retail Park, West Thurrock Way, on Saturday 21 November 2026, the trade titles Retail Times and Furniture News report. The store covers 975 sq m across a ground floor and mezzanine, roughly a seventh of a football pitch.

The firm was founded in Sydney in 1977, designs, makes and sells its own furniture, and now trades in eight countries. Alongside sofas, the West Thurrock store will show dining furniture, its King Sleep beds, outdoor designs, lighting and rugs, with more than 200 fabric and leather options.
Stu Mangan will manage the showroom, which the company expects to draw customers from across Essex, east London and the wider South East. King Living marks its 50th anniversary in 2027.
points: Founded in Sydney in 1977, trading in eight countries
More than 200 fabric and leather options
Showroom manager: Stu Mangan

stories.headline: Braintree MP Cleverly targets Khan on crime and housing in mayor bid
stories.summary: Sir James Cleverly took 86% of London Conservative members' votes on 19 November. Braintree's Conservatives must now find a new parliamentary candidate.
body: Sir James Cleverly, MP for Braintree since 2015, was chosen on Thursday 19 November as the Conservative candidate for the London mayoral election in May 2028. The former foreign secretary and home secretary told LBC he was "all in" for the contest.

He beat Westminster City councillor Festus Akinbusoye and Sara Gezdari, a former parliamentary candidate in Richmond Park, the BBC reports. Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch, his rival for the party leadership in 2024, congratulated him. Labour chair Bridget Phillipson said he should not be trusted with the capital.

After his selection, Sir James attacked Labour mayor Lord Khan's record on crime and housing. He said people are leaving London or choosing not to move there. Lord Khan has not said whether he will seek a fourth term. Reform UK has already named Laila Cunningham as its candidate.
points: Rivals: Festus Akinbusoye and Sara Gezdari
Kemi Badenoch congratulated him; Labour's Bridget Phillipson attacked his record
Reform UK has already picked Laila Cunningham

stories.headline: Stansted owner's survey puts east ahead for export growth
stories.summary: Six in 10 exporters in the East of England, which includes Essex, grew overseas sales between July and September, the best of four regions in a survey commissioned by London Stansted's owner MAG.
body: The East of England led four UK regions for export growth in the third quarter of 2026, according to the UK Trade Barometer published by London Stansted's owner, Manchester Airports Group (MAG), on Thursday 19 November. The quarterly YouGov survey of more than 2,000 firms, run with the Growing Together Alliance of business groups, found 42% of the region's exporters had started selling in a new country, level with London.
The US was the region's top growth market, followed by France and Australia.
points: London ranked second at 59%, ahead of the Midlands and the North
19% of the region's exporters grew sales to the US
Only 11% expect to enter a new market by December

stories.headline: M11 southbound reopens near Stansted after two-lorry crash
stories.summary: National Highways has reopened the motorway between Duxford and Bishop's Stortford, ending a closure of about 25 hours that sent drivers heading into Essex on a long detour through Hertfordshire.
body: The carriageway between junction 10 at Duxford and junction 8 for Bishop's Stortford and Stansted Airport was open again at 6.36am on Thursday 19 November, National Highways said, the Bishop's Stortford Independent reports. It had been shut since two lorries collided at about 5.40am the day before, leaving one straddling the roadside barrier.

Essex County Fire and Rescue Service was called at 5.48am on Wednesday 18 November and sent crews from Newport; nobody was hurt or trapped, and firefighters left at 7.27am. Fuel and debris spread across a long stretch of the road, and recovery of the wreckage went on into Wednesday night with no reopening time given.

While the road was shut, the signed diversion left at junction 10 and followed the A505, A10 and A120 through Royston, Buntingford and Standon to rejoin the M11 at junction 8. Drivers faced delays of up to 90 minutes on the approach on the Wednesday morning.
points: Crash happened at about 5.40am on Wednesday 18 November
No one was hurt or trapped, the fire service said
The diversion ran via the A505, A10 and A120
stories.source: Essex County Fire and Rescue Service

stories.headline: London Gateway systems fault queues lorries back to A13 Manorway
stories.summary: Link roads in Stanford-le-Hope and Corringham backed up as trucks waited to get into the DP World port in Thurrock.
body: A quayside systems issue at DP World London Gateway on the morning of Thursday 19 November 2026 left lorries queuing back to the A13 Manorway roundabout, Thurrock Nub News reports. At 11.45am the port said its terminal operating system was stable and it was working through the backlog of trucks. c2c also warned of delays and cancellations that morning because of problems between Pitsea and Southend.
points: Four container ships were at berth
Port said at 11.45am that terminal operations were working as expected

stories.headline: Harlow Council plans tougher line on landlords who let unsafe homes
stories.summary: Harlow tenants living with damp, mould or missing smoke alarms would see the council move straight to formal action against their landlords under a new policy.
body: Harlow Council's cabinet is due to approve a Private Sector Housing Enforcement Policy that puts formal enforcement first once a breach of landlord law is found in Harlow, Your Harlow reported on 19 November. Officers would run targeted inspections aimed at serious hazards, repeat offenders and vulnerable tenants.

Landlords who ignore a notice to fix a missing or faulty smoke or carbon monoxide alarm would face a £3,000 penalty, rising to £5,000 for a repeat. Council leader Dan Swords said renters should be able to report problems without fear of losing their home.
points: Up to £4,000 for unlawfully letting energy-inefficient homes
Penalty income to be reinvested in enforcement
Banning orders and rent repayment orders possible in serious cases

stories.headline: Basildon house prices hit record average of £367,920
stories.summary: Land Registry figures for September put the Basildon borough's average just £11 above its November 2022 peak, Basildon Today reports.
body: Prices in the Basildon borough rose 0.8% over the year, against an Essex average of £360,791. The index came out on 18 November. Flats were the only type of home to fall in value over the year. The latest months are often revised as late sales are registered, so the record could slip.
points: First-time buyers paid an average of £307,721
Castle Point's average is now £271 above Basildon's
Flats fell 1.6% over the year

stories.headline: Basildon council homes audit cannot confirm hazards were fixed
stories.summary: An independent check of Basildon Council's 11,790 homes found no council-wide system for tracking hazards such as damp, mould and cold, months after the housing regulator gave it the lowest grade.
body: Auditors from Pennington Choices, who carried out the review in September 2026, said they could not get enough evidence that every hazard found had been dealt with, because records are deleted once work is finished, Basildon Today reports.

The Housing Ombudsman made 32 findings of maladministration against Basildon Council in 2025/26. Councillors on the Housing Scrutiny Committee will discuss the audit at 7pm on Wednesday 25 November 2026.
points: Regulator of Social Housing gave Basildon a C4 grade in April
11 recommendations, one rated critical
£13,299 in compensation ordered or recommended by the ombudsman

stories.headline: Basildon council tenants face up to £1 a week extra rent from April
stories.summary: The charge, on top of the usual inflation-linked rise, would grow to up to £2 a week each year from April 2028 until rents reach the government's formula level.
body: About three quarters of Basildon Council's social rents are below formula rent, the level set by government. The council wants to close that gap, starting in April 2027 with an extra charge on top of the standard rise of inflation plus 1%, Basildon Today reports from council papers.

Council papers warn the housing account is at risk of not being able to set a balanced budget, pointing to past rent cuts and caps, safety costs and the age of the New Town's homes. An October draft had said existing tenants would see only the annual government increase.
points: Expected to raise about £500,000 a year for the housing account
About 5,600 tenants, around half, get help with housing costs
Cabinet decides at 7pm on Thursday 26 November

stories.summary: Chris Hodson of Pitman Training in Essex blames wage rates, employment taxes and welfare, not a shortage of job schemes, for young people being out of work.
body: Alan Milburn's national review of young people not in education, employment or training drew criticism from Essex business voices on 19 November, Business Wire Essex reports. Chris Hodson, programme director at Pitman Training in Essex, said it showed a fundamental lack of understanding of how jobs are created. Peter Richardson, publishing editor of BusinessTime in Essex, backed him, arguing that businesses, not governments, create jobs.
points: The review aims to cut the national Neet rate to about 5% within a decade
It proposes employer grants of up to £3,000 for hiring young people

stories.summary: Spare rooms on the Colchester campus could go to Ministry of Defence personnel, BBC News reports.

Talks with the MoD are continuing

stories.headline: Chelmsford's Sandon School raffles prizes to keep GTA 6 fans in class
stories.summary: A secondary school near Chelmsford is entering pupils who attend into a prize draw, after the long-awaited video game's UK release.
body: Sandon School's prizes for turning up on Thursday 19 and Friday 20 November include £10 Amazon vouchers, free Christmas dinners and a lunchtime queue-jump pass for the rest of the school year, the BBC reports. A letter to parents says time off to play the game in school hours will count as an unauthorised absence.
Head teacher Jon Pead said the school was not expecting half-empty classrooms. In Halstead, The Ramsey Academy is offering sweet treats and extra house points to pupils who come in.

Absences to play the game count as unauthorised
Halstead's Ramsey Academy is handing out house points for attendance

stories.headline: BAE Systems, with Great Baddow base, plans up to 1,070 UK job cuts
stories.summary: The defence company says the cuts will fall on its UK head office and air sector, out of about 50,000 UK employees.
body: BAE Systems announced on Wednesday 18 November that it will seek the reductions through a voluntary process and work with trade unions, the Evening Standard reports. Shopfloor manufacturing, aircraft maintenance at RAF bases and early careers trainees are excluded.

Unite general secretary Sharon Graham blamed delays in defence spending and called for new contracts for British-built aircraft. The Echo reports that the company has not confirmed whether staff at Great Baddow, Chelmsford, are affected.

Unite wants contracts for British-built Typhoons

stories.headline: Driver jailed for 81mph Theydon Bois crash that killed pedestrian
stories.summary: A North Weald man who lost control of his car on the B172 Abridge Road near Theydon Bois, killing a 59-year-old Basildon man walking at the roadside, has been jailed for six years and nine months.
body: Stuart Wagner, 29, of Blenheim Square, North Weald, admitted causing death by dangerous driving and was sentenced at Chelmsford Crown Court on Thursday 5 November, Your Harlow reports. He was also banned from driving for eight years and four months.

The crash happened shortly before 6.30pm on Monday 21 July 2025, after Wagner overtook two cars and lost control of his BMW M4 on a bend. Mr Skeels was walking facing traffic where there is no pavement and died at the scene.

Crash on Monday 21 July 2025
Speed found by the Serious Collision Investigation Unit

body: Thurrock Council's planning committee voted 6-2 in July to reject the part-retrospective application, against its officers' advice to approve it, Your Thurrock reports. Ward councillor Aaron Green is urging residents to send their views to the inspector, citing lorry traffic, road safety, noise and air pollution.

Plans also include hardstanding repairs and acoustic fencing

stories.headline: Billericay community awards draw more than 20,000 public votes
stories.summary: Cloud 9 Espresso Bar, the High Street Post Office and volunteer Mark Thomas were among 10 winners named at Billericay's second community awards.
body: The Your Billericay Business Improvement District handed out its 2026 awards at Cristi's Bar on Billericay High Street on Tuesday 17 November, with Great British Bake Off contestant Andy Ryan as host, Your Thurrock reports.

Votes rose on the first year of the awards in 2025, which drew more than 15,000. Other winners included K Barbers Emporium, Creatures Great & Small for customer care and The Olive Branch for its window display.

stories.headline: Saffron Walden lights switch-on brings Market Place party on Friday
stories.summary: Father Christmas will switch on Saffron Walden's Christmas lights at 6pm on Friday 20 November, with music, food stalls and pantomime cast members in the Market Place from 3pm.
body: Six town centre streets in Saffron Walden, including King Street, Market Hill and Cross Street, will be closed from 7am to 11pm on Friday 20 November to make room for the celebrations, the town council's tourist information centre says.

Stuart Vant returns as host, with performances from LP Chorus Collective, Somewhere 2 Sing and Tempo's Performing Arts, free face painting, and cast members from Saffron Hall's pantomime, Sleeping Beauty, leading the countdown. Stalls will sell bagels, wood-fired pizza, Greek food, cakes and hot drinks, alongside a licensed bar.

Town Mayor Cllr Curtis will run a tombola, with prizes partly given by local businesses, raising money for Together in Sound, The Garden Youth Music Project and Teenage Kicks. The entertainment carries on until 7.30pm.
points: Host: Stuart Vant
Mayor's tombola supports three local youth and music charities
Roads reopen at 11pm

stories.summary: Harlow Council has made a jokey video in the style of Grand Theft Auto VI. It takes viewers round the town's roundabouts and rebuilt Market Square.
body: The council put the video out on Wednesday 18 November, the day before the game went on sale, Your Harlow reports. It uses the game's look to promote new homes, rebuilt neighbourhoods and the multi-million-pound overhaul of the town centre. Council leader Dan Swords said Harlow deserved the 'blockbuster treatment' because so much is changing. He said people could see the changes just by stepping outside their front door.

Council leader Dan Swords fronted the launch

stories.headline: Colchester to get US chicken chain Raising Cane's first UK drive-thru
stories.summary: Colchester is one of four new UK sites named by the American fried chicken chain, with the restaurant due to open in 2028.
body: The drive-thru was added to the Raising Cane's UK pipeline on Wednesday 18 November alongside Bishopsgate in London, Watford and Manchester, trade title Restaurant Online reports. No address in Colchester has been given yet.
The chain opens its UK flagship near Piccadilly Circus in spring 2027, with more London restaurants to follow that year.

Planned UK estate now eight restaurants

stories.headline: Southend seafront to get new public toilets in £750,000 plan
stories.summary: Southend-on-Sea City Council's cabinet has backed the spending, which comes from outside the council, after a review of the city's public toilets.
body: A large new toilet block is planned for Marine Parade in Southend, with a second facility serving the eastern seafront, under plans the cabinet approved on Monday 16 November. Southend-on-Sea City Council announced the decision on Wednesday 18 November.

The plans follow a city-wide review of public toilets and feedback from nearly 500 residents and visitors, 94% of whom said new seafront toilets were important or very important. Money will also go on improving existing toilets, their upkeep and accessibility, and the council says several other seafront sites are being considered. Its announcement does not name the funder.

Councillor Cheryl Nevin, cabinet member for civic pride, said clean and accessible toilets make 'a real difference to people's day-to-day lives'. Detailed design and delivery plans come next, and no start date has been given.
points: Nearly 500 people gave feedback in the toilet review
94% rated new seafront toilets important or very important
No start date yet: detailed design comes next

stories.headline: Essex police commissioner joins 30 others urging PM to halt force mergers
stories.summary: Roger Hirst is one of 31 commissioners and deputy mayors from several parties asking the Government to drop plans for big regional police forces.
body: The letter to the Prime Minister was published on 16 November and coordinated by Kent's police and crime commissioner, Matthew Scott, according to the Essex Police, Fire and Crime Commissioner's office. It urges ministers to scrap forced mergers that would turn the 43 police forces in England and Wales into about nine regional forces.

Mr Hirst, the Police, Fire and Crime Commissioner for Essex, said: "Policing relies on public consent and, importantly, on public confidence and trust." His office points to its own survey of more than 1,700 people, run from 10 June to 22 July 2026. In it, 69% opposed merging forces into larger regional bodies.

The same survey found 86% wanted Essex to keep a strong local police presence, and 85% said local policing should stay locally led. The Government has not yet published its final decision on the shape of policing. Mr Hirst first set out his opposition to a regional force for the east earlier in November.
points: Letter coordinated by Kent commissioner Matthew Scott
Plan would cut 43 forces to about 9
Survey: 86% want a strong local police presence in Essex
stories.source: Essex Police, Fire and Crime Commissioner
stories.newAngle: Roger Hirst signed a joint letter of 31 commissioners to the Prime Minister on 16 November.

stories.headline: Essex water firm adds 30% more leak crews as reservoirs stay low
stories.summary: Essex & Suffolk Water says supplies across mid and south Essex are not at risk, but wants customers to keep saving water through the winter while the hosepipe ban stays in place.
body: Hanningfield Reservoir near Chelmsford was 35% full and Abberton near Colchester 38% full when BBC News reported the figures on Wednesday 18 November, against averages of 69% and 62% for the time of year. Rain across Essex from May to October came to only 61% of the seasonal average.

Essex & Suffolk Water is stepping up its drought response, and water director Kieran Ingram said: 'Summer may be over, but the drought isn't.' The company is asking customers to take shorter showers, turn taps off, run washing machines and dishwashers only when full, and fix dripping taps and leaking toilets. It says its leak repair workforce has grown by 30% and that it fixed more leaks in the first 10 months of 2026 than in the whole of 2025.

The Temporary Use Ban, in force since 3 August, has cut demand by about 7% and remains in place, and the company's own figures put combined storage at 37% on 17 November, below average. Mr Ingram said the coming winter would largely decide the position for spring and summer 2027, and the Environment Agency says some parts of England need 120% of normal rainfall over the next six months to recover.
points: Combined storage stood at 37% on 17 November, the company's own figures show
Hosepipe ban in force since 3 August has cut demand by about 7%
Abberton was 38% full against a 62% average for the time of year

stories.headline: Harlow College shuts for the day after power cut
stories.summary: Students at Harlow College's Velizy Avenue campus were told to stay away because the site had lost its electricity supply.
body: Harlow College announced on Wednesday 18 November that it had closed because of a power outage, Your Harlow reports. BMAT STEM Academy stayed open.
points: BMAT STEM Academy stayed open
Your Harlow reported the closure at 10.13am

stories.headline: Shoebury toddler Blake, 17 months, remembered as police inquiry continues
stories.summary: Blake Branch died after ambulance crews raised concerns for a child's welfare at a Shoeburyness home in October. Detectives investigating his death have two people on conditional bail.
body: Essex Police released the little boy's name and his family's tribute on Wednesday 18 November, five weeks after officers were called to an address in Eagle Way, Shoeburyness. Ambulance crews had raised concerns for a child's welfare there just before 8am on Monday 12 October, and detectives opened an investigation after Blake died.

"My precious little boy was loved more than words could ever explain," his family said. They said they longed for one more cuddle with him, and thanked everyone who has shown them kindness and support.

A 24-year-old man from Rayleigh and a 26-year-old woman from Shoeburyness were arrested as part of the investigation into Blake's death. Both are on conditional bail while enquiries continue, Essex Police said, and the family have asked for privacy while the investigation takes its course.
points: Officers were called to Eagle Way just before 8am on 12 October
Essex Police released his name and the family's tribute on 18 November
His family have asked for privacy

stories.headline: Southend's Palace Hotel to switch from Radisson to IHG's Garner brand
stories.summary: The Southend hotel, which trades as the Park Inn Palace, can already be booked on IHG's website as an independent property.
body: The Palace Hotel in Southend-on-Sea is leaving Radisson and is due to become a Garner, the budget conversion brand of InterContinental Hotels Group, in 2027, the travel website Head for Points reported on 18 November. The site expects the change once the upgrades the brand requires have been made.
points: Garner is IHG's budget conversion brand

stories.headline: South Ockendon school trust keeps pupils' Christmas events as it reviews visits
stories.summary: The Catalyst Academies Trust, which runs Benyon Primary and five other Thurrock schools, says it is close to new arrangements that would let more relatives attend Christmas performances.

stories.headline: Whatever happened to Loughton's £2bn data centre?
stories.summary: It was originally due to open before the end of 2026. Instead Microsoft has pulled out, the electricity is years away and Nscale has no new date for its AI site.
body: Britain's biggest artificial intelligence data centre was supposed to be running in Loughton by now. Nscale bought a scaffolding yard on Langston Road, near Debden station, in January 2025 and said the site would be operating by the last quarter of 2026. Ministers later held it up as the country's largest sovereign AI project. Six weeks before the year ends, the yard has been cleared but there is no data centre. The Times this week described the plot as "a pile of bricks".

The obstacle is electricity. The site was due to receive its supply by the end of this year, the BBC reports, but Nscale has been told a connection will not come until the next decade. The Guardian reported in September that UK Power Networks had put the date at the early to mid 2030s. In October Microsoft, the only customer announced for Loughton and the firm due to rent about 23,000 Nvidia chips there, ended its agreement. "This decision relates to a single site," a Microsoft spokesperson told Data Centre Review. Nscale told the BBC: "We remain committed to both the Loughton project and the UK." It says it is exploring other sources of power for the site.

For Loughton, the promise was work: Nscale said about 500 jobs in construction and a further 250 permanent roles once the centre opened. The scheme was never universally welcome. Loughton Town Council officers objected in March, asking for evidence that its energy demand would not strain the local grid or push up residents' bills. Epping Forest District Council approved a larger design in June over objections from councillors and residents, after investment minister Lord Stockwood wrote to the council's chief executive to stress the government's support. Nscale has not given a new opening date.

University Hospitals of Morecambe Bay had the highest total with 242, followed by West Suffolk with 213 and Northumbria Healthcare with 195, PA found. body: Professor Tracy Lawson, of the University of Essex School of Life Sciences in Colchester, is on Clarivate's Highly Cited Researchers list for the seventh year running, the university announced on Wednesday 18 November. Professor Reinhard Pekrun, of the Department of Psychology, has appeared in every edition since 2024.

Professor Lawson develops ways of measuring how plants photosynthesise and use water, helping researchers find traits that could make crops cope better with heat and drought. Professor Pekrun's work looks at how enjoyment, anxiety and boredom shape students' motivation and results. Clarivate estimates that about one in every 1,000 scientists and social scientists worldwide makes the list.

This year Clarivate gave 7,090 designations to 6,802 researchers at more than 1,200 institutions in 62 countries and regions, judged on how often other researchers cited their papers from 2015 to 2025. Professor Noam Lubell, the university's Pro-Vice-Chancellor for Research, called it a brilliant achievement for the two academics.

body: Dr Haider Raza, a senior lecturer in the University of Essex's School of Computer Science and Electronic Engineering, has been named on Universities UK's first 50 Future Innovators list, published on Tuesday.

Working with Cambridge screening company Check4Cancer through a Knowledge Transfer Partnership, he helped create SKINTEL, which combines image analysis with 22 patient characteristics, such as age, skin tone, hair colour and family history, to judge whether a suspicious lesion is malignant. It is designed to support doctors rather than replace them, speeding up diagnosis and catching the most dangerous lesions at the earliest stage.
"I'm honoured to be recognised," Dr Raza said, adding that he wanted to show how "trustworthy and explainable AI can deliver real-world impact in healthcare".
Professor Noam Lubell, the university's pro-vice-chancellor for research, said the work had the potential to transform skin cancer diagnostics around the world.

Universities UK, which represents more than 140 universities, chose the 50 from more than 300 nominations, with Baroness Martha Lane Fox among the independent judges. The list is part of its campaign to double outside investment in university innovation to £100bn by 2035.

stories.headline: Nearly 100 Colchester households stuck in B&Bs as housing demand climbs

points: The city is above its own target for households in temporary accommodation

body: Colchester had 588 households in temporary accommodation at the end of September, 98 of them in bed and breakfasts, according to the council's latest quarterly housing report, which goes before councillors shortly. The total was 550 three months earlier and 472 in mid-November last year, a rise of almost a quarter, the Daily Gazette reports. It puts the city at seven households in temporary accommodation for every 1,000, above the council's own target of six.

The council's half-year performance report, discussed by its scrutiny panel on 11 November and due before cabinet on 2 December, says 616 households facing homelessness were being supported by 31 October. Council leader Paul Dundas said demand for housing "remains extremely high". The pressure has built quickly: the council's own figures showed 326 households in temporary accommodation in March 2024 and 449 a year later, while Colchester Borough Homes, which runs the city's homelessness service, assessed 1,563 new homelessness cases in 2024/25.

The council has turned former private student flats into temporary homes, a scheme that won a bronze award at the Local Government Chronicle awards in June, and plans to buy 65 homes during 2026/27 to cut its reliance on costly temporary accommodation. It has previously said it uses B&Bs only when it is urgent and for short periods. Nationally, the government has committed to ending the unlawful use of B&Bs for families, and a new Colchester homelessness and rough sleeping strategy for 2026 to 2031 aims to step in before households reach crisis point.

body: Tendring District Council's cabinet agreed on Friday 13 November 2026 to consult on a change to its Local Council Tax Support scheme for 2027/28. The change would let working-age claimants have their claims backdated by up to 3 months. The council must first consult the major preceptors, the other public bodies that set a share of the council tax bill.

The report to the cabinet says the scheme already lets pension-age claimants backdate claims by 3 months. It says a few recent working-age cases would have benefited from the same help where there was good cause, such as clear proof they were eligible before they applied. The rest of the scheme stays as it is, including a maximum discount of 80% for working-age claimants.

A draft scheme goes back to the cabinet on Friday 11 December 2026. The Resources and Services Overview and Scrutiny Committee will look at it before Full Council decides in January 2027. The cabinet also recommended keeping the 100% council tax premium on second homes and the current premiums on long-term empty homes.

councilwatch.summary: Repairs and damp and mould work also leave Basildon's council housing account forecast to finish £3.2m over budget in 2026/27, according to a report for the council's Cabinet.
body: Basildon Borough Council's Cabinet will be asked on Thursday 26 November 2026 to note that its General Fund, which pays for most day-to-day services, is forecast to end the year £3.8 million over budget. The forecast, based on spending to the end of September, has grown by £400,000 since the first quarter of the year.

The report blames the cost of the temporary accommodation the council must provide for homeless households, and in particular a shortage of alternatives to expensive nightly paid accommodation. Capital financing, staffing and the risk that planned savings are not delivered add to the pressure, partly offset by extra planning income. On the Housing Revenue Account, which covers council homes, the position has improved by £1.3 million since the first quarter, with the report pointing to rising repair costs, damp and mould cases and the cost of meeting a Regulatory Notice from the Regulator of Social Housing.

The report says any pressures that cannot be managed by the end of the financial year will have to be met from the council's revenue reserves. Services must now set out the actions they are taking each month under a formal recovery plan process, which officers say is showing early signs of working. The revenue figures went to the Finance, Procurement and Efficiency Scrutiny Committee on 16 November 2026 and will feed into setting future budgets.

The Director of Finance's report for the six months to 30 September says most appeals cost around £100,000 each and five are expected to be heard in 2026/27.

councilwatch.summary: Community groups wanting to take over a Maldon District Council building or plot would have to show public benefit, local support and sound finances under the draft policy.
body: Maldon District Council's Strategy and Resources Committee will consider an Asset Disposal Policy on Thursday 26 November 2026, setting out how requests to buy or take over council-owned land and property across the district will be judged. The report from the Director of Neighbourhood Services and Communities recommends that councillors approve it.

The policy sets out three routes: sale on the open market, sale to a special purchaser and Community Asset Transfer. Each request would go through stages including initial assessment, due diligence, an options appraisal, independent valuation and engagement before approval and legal completion, and the council could use restrictive covenants, overage and clawback clauses to protect its interests. Applicants or buyers would normally pay the council's legal and professional costs.

Requests would not normally go ahead if the council still needs the asset, if a substantially similar request was decided in the previous six months, or if the application fails the criteria. Any sale or lease of a large site would still need approval from Full Council, and the report says the financial effect of individual disposals would be set out in future reports.
